title: Scalar extension to all-continuous algebraic-closure coefficients preserves bounded constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the extended norm topologies on $E$ and $\Omega$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On profinite sets put $A(P)=C(P,E)$ and $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, using ALL continuous functions, and let $A\to B$ be induced by the inclusion $E\subseteq\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Let $Z$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]) and put $A_Z=p_Z^*A$, $B_Z=p_Z^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module objects, ordinary unbounded derived categories and the ordinary K-flat derived scalar extension $T_Z=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-:D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_Z})\to D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_Z})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. For $G=E,\Omega$ with coefficient ring $R=A,B$, call a complex of $R_Z$-modules bounded constructible if its cohomology is bounded and each cohomology module, on the pieces of a finite stratification of $Z$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], is pro-etale locally $R\otimes_GV$ for a finite-dimensional $G$-vector space $V$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model].

Then $T_Z$ sends every bounded constructible complex of $A_Z$-modules to a bounded constructible complex of $B_Z$-modules, and that image has finite Tor amplitude over $B_Z$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. More precisely, let $c:S\hookrightarrow Z$ be a constructible locally closed immersion, factored as an open immersion $j$ into its closure followed by the closed immersion $i$, with $c_!=i_*j_!$ the exact coefficient-module functors [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement], and let $L$ be a lisse finite-rank $A_S$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Then $B_S\otimes_{A_S}L$ is a lisse finite-rank $B_S$-module, equal to $B_S^r$ wherever $L\cong A_S^r$ (including $r=0$), and the canonical support-projection and unit-normalized pullback/tensor comparisons give an isomorphism $T_Z(c_!L[0])\cong c_!(B_S\otimes_{A_S}L)[0]$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_Z})$. Flatness of $A\to B$, completeness of $\Omega$, and a finite-subextension-valued replacement of $B$ are not assumed.

proof.text: Apply locally-free derived scalars on $S$ to $R=A_S$, $M=L$, and $R\to B_S$. It gives a natural canonical isomorphism $T_S(L[0])\cong L_B[0]$, with $L_B=B_S\otimes_{A_S}L$ lisse of the same local ranks. On a rank-$r$ chart the map is $b\otimes(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\mapsto(ba_1,\ldots,ba_r)$, with inverse $(b_k)\mapsto\sum_kb_k\otimes e_k$. Thus $r=0$ is included. In particular $L[0]$ and $L_B[0]$ are K-flat over their respective coefficient rings. Only local freeness is used, not flatness of $A\to B$.

proof.text:
Write $c=i\circ j$ with $j:S\hookrightarrow C=\overline S$ and $i:C\hookrightarrow Z$. Apply the closed support formula to $(i,Z\setminus C)$, then the inverse open formula to $(C\setminus S,j)$. Both are complementary pairs in Noetherian schemes; their opens are quasi-compact, as required. With coefficient $A$ and tensor argument $B_Z[0]$, tensor symmetry gives
$$B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}i_*j_!L\cong i_*j_!(c^*B_Z\otimes^L_{A_S}L).$$
The Cartesian isomorphisms for both $A$ and $B$ identify this with $c_!T_S(L[0])$. Step 1 gives the asserted $c_!L_B[0]$. Exact functors here act termwise; no unbounded right-derived image is needed. The normalization lemma identifies the pullback/tensor comparison with its unit-preserving balancing map. The support maps are the specified unit/counit maps. They are $B$-linear: multiplication on the tensor factor commutes with balancing and projection, $b'(b\otimes l)=(b'b)\otimes l$. Thus the composite lies in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_Z})$.

proof.text: Every target generator $c_!L_B[0]$ is bounded constructible by the all-continuous-$\Omega$ generator theorem. For any degree-zero $B_Z$-module $N$, apply both support projections now with coefficient ring $B$ to get $(c_!L_B[0])\otimes^L_{B_Z}N[0]\cong c_!(L_B[0]\otimes^L_{B_S}c^*N[0])$. By step 1, $L_B$ is flat and K-flat; thus the inner tensor is $(L_B\otimes_{B_S}c^*N)[0]$. The exactness of $c^*$ and $c_!$ makes the right side concentrated in degree zero. This proves Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ for each generator against every module $N$, including nonconstructible ones.

proof.text: Apply the finite-$E$ generation theorem only to the source coefficient $A$: every bounded constructible $K$ has a finite construction from supported lisse generators using shifts and cones. Derived change of rings is an exact triangulated functor for every ring-sheaf map, so $T_Z$ carries that construction to the same shifts and cones of the images from step 2. The all-continuous-$\Omega$ generator theorem gives a replete triangulated bounded constructible target subcategory, so step 3 implies bounded constructibility of $T_ZK$. Finite Tor amplitude forms a thick subcategory by the cited Tor-amplitude statement. Explicitly, start generators with interval $[0,0]$; shift by $n$ changes $[a,b]$ to $[a-n,b-n]$, and the cone of objects with intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ has interval $[\min(c,a-1),\max(d,b-1)]$, by rotating the triangle and enlarging intervals. Finitely many operations give a finite interval for this $K$. The empty scheme, zero complex and rank-zero generators give zero.
